_meta.note: 19 user-supplied links. NET-NEW MODEL FAMILY: IFM (Institute of Foundation Models, MBZUAI) K2 Horizon, released 2026-09-03 and billed as the largest fully open-source launch to date — six models (375B-A23B and MoVA-36B-A4B MoE, 32B dense, 7B, 3.7B, 0.9B) with open training code and data. All six benchmark tables were parsed from the blog's HTML <table> markup rather than a text dump, since the flattened text scrambles header/value alignment. Only the K2 columns are ingested; vendor-selected comparison columns are skipped because those models already carry primary-source rows. NEW BENCHMARKS: Conceptual Reasoning Index (Anthropic Alignment; LMCA 60% + ACCoRD 20% + DTBench 20%), Terminal-Bench 4.0 (66 tasks, distinct id from terminal_bench_2_1 because the task set differs), Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 (70 scientist-authored tasks), NYT Connections Extended (940 puzzles, quadratic-v1), and three SRE-Bench paper metrics. KEY ID DECISION: arXiv 2608.11469 turns out to be the SRE-Bench paper (Vals AI is a co-author), i.e. the same benchmark as the `sre_bench` id created in S261 from OpenAI's card. The two use different protocols — OpenAI reports pass@4 (Astra 99.2 / Sol 68.7) while the paper reports pass@1 capability score (Sol 61.4) — so the paper's numbers go to separate ids instead of being mixed into one series. CROSS-VALIDATION: BenchLM's ARC-AGI-3 board independently matches the DB after the S263 ARC-AGI-1/3 correction (Astra 62.7, Opus 5 30.2, Sol 7.8, Terra 0.8), confirming that fix; 5 models absent from the DB were added. NOT INGESTED: RuneBench (framework described but the page carries no results table), Perplexity WANDR (HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and curl), the four x.com links (blocked), the HuggingFace collection and orcarouter comparison post (no primary numbers beyond what the vendor blog already provides), openai.com/index/gpt-6-astra (already mined in S260-S260c), and arXiv 2609.04148 Terminal-Universe, whose result tables are dominated by research SFT checkpoints (TerminalTraj-32B, TermiGen-32B, ...) that fall outside the latest-models-focus rule.

benchmarks.name: Conceptual Reasoning Index (CRI)
benchmarks.description: Anthropic Alignment Science aggregate measuring reasoning about questions that lack empirical verification (AI governance, alignment, decision theory). Weighted average of LMCA (60%), ACCoRD (20%) and DTBench capabilities (20%). 0-100, with an estimated ceiling near 91.

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench 4.0 (resolution rate)
benchmarks.description: Terminal-Bench v4.0.0 (Aug 2026): 66 tasks after removing 8 and revising 20 from v3.0. Measures whether an agent can operate a real terminal for software-engineering and systems tasks. Separate id from terminal_bench_2_1 because the task set differs (2.x had 89 tasks).

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1
benchmarks.description: 70 terminal-agent tasks across the life, physical, Earth, mathematical and engineering sciences, contributed and peer-reviewed by practising scientists for scientific validity and realism. NOTE: this id mixes two reporting channels — the official announcement leaderboard and vendor self-reports. Anthropic's Fable 5.1 system card self-reports 52.6, well above the official board's top entry (Opus 5, 30.0), and Fable 5.1 does not appear on that board; compare across channels with care.

benchmarks.name: NYT Connections — Extended (quadratic-v1)
benchmarks.description: 940 NYT Connections puzzles with up to four extra trick words added per puzzle. Quadratic-v1 scoring: a puzzle with g exact groups contributes (g/4)^2, so 0/1/2/3/4 groups earn 0 / 6.25 / 25 / 56.25 / 100%.

benchmarks.name: SRE-Bench — capability score (paper, pass@1)
benchmarks.description: SRE-Bench (Columbia / UC Berkeley / Vals AI / Tufts, arXiv 2608.11469): 262 contamination-free reverse-engineering instances, 1,572 deterministically verifiable tasks (6 objectives each). Standardised mini-SWE-agent harness whose only tool is bash, max reasoning effort, 500 steps / 6h cap. NOTE: kept separate from the `sre_bench` id, which holds OpenAI's own pass@4 figures from the GPT-6 Astra card (Astra 99.2 / Sol 68.7) — a different protocol and a different scale.

benchmarks.name: SRE-Bench — instances fully solved (6/6)
benchmarks.description: SRE-Bench (Columbia / UC Berkeley / Vals AI / Tufts, arXiv 2608.11469): 262 contamination-free reverse-engineering instances, 1,572 deterministically verifiable tasks (6 objectives each). Standardised mini-SWE-agent harness whose only tool is bash, max reasoning effort, 500 steps / 6h cap. NOTE: kept separate from the `sre_bench` id, which holds OpenAI's own pass@4 figures from the GPT-6 Astra card (Astra 99.2 / Sol 68.7) — a different protocol and a different scale.

NOTE: kept separate from the `sre_bench` id, which holds OpenAI's own pass@4 figures from the GPT-6 Astra card (Astra 99.2 / Sol 68.7) — a different protocol and a different scale. Lower is better.
